For referencing: "Because Getis-Ord predicts a variable-length set of boroughs per chunk, both micro-averaged (pooled across all borough-chunk pairs)
 and macro-averaged (computed per chunk, then averaged) precision/recall/F1 are reported, following standard multi-label evaluation practice (Sokolova & Lapalme, 2009; Tsoumakas & Katakis, 2007)."

Since ground truth for this task is a set of significant boroughs rather than a single label, requiring an exact set match penalizes near-correct answers as harshly as completely wrong ones — a model that correctly identifies 4 of 5 real hot spots scores identically to one that finds none at all. Jaccard-based accuracy (|predicted ? real| / |predicted ? real|) instead measures the genuine degree of overlap between prediction and ground truth, rewarding partial correctness proportionally while still penalizing both missed hot spots and spurious false positives (since both enlarge the union without enlarging the intersection). This is a standard, established approach for multi-label classification — commonly termed example-based accuracy (Godbole & Sarawagi, 2004)
